4The end p.108

  • Success: enough successes in time. You get what you asked.
  • Failure: some successes, not enough. A plain no, or (if the Loremaster agrees) success at a price: less help, a new enemy, trouble later.
  • Disaster: every roll failed, or the talk fell short after a failed introduction. The hosts now see the Company as a threat.

His story

A farm lad from Bree-land who dreams of drawing maps. A year ago a storm scared off Tin, his masked donkey, and Tom has followed the trail ever since. He tells sad stories about why the donkey matters so much. The stories never match, and that is the joke.

Experience before play

Before play he raised Stealth from 1 to 3 (5 points) and Scan from 1 to 3 (5 points).

Words of the game

Loremasterthe game master

The person who runs the game and plays the world, the people and the enemies.

Companythe group of heroes

Tom and his friends. The Company shares the Fellowship pool.

Culture and Callingwho Tom is and what drives him

Culture = his people (Men of Bree). Calling = his drive, a bit like a class (Treasure Hunter).

TNTarget Number

The number a roll must reach: 20 minus the attribute. Tom: Strength 16, Heart 16, Wits 13 p.18.

Adventuring and Fellowship phasesplay and rest

Play goes back and forth: adventures, then a long rest in a safe place p.118.

Rolling dice

The dice1 Feat die + 1 Success die per rank

Every roll uses the Feat die (12 faces) and one Success die (6 faces) per rank in the skill. Rank 0: the Feat die alone p.17.

Successreach the TN

Add all the dice. Reach the TN and the roll succeeds p.17. Usually there is one try; the Loremaster may allow another with a different skill.

Rune and Eyethe two picture faces

Rune: automatic success. Eye: counts as 0 p.17.

Iconsa 6 on a Success die

On a success, 1 icon = great success, 2 or more = extraordinary. Icons can buy small extras: quieter, faster, learn more p.18 p.19.

Favoured and Ill-favoured2 Feat dice

Favoured: roll 2 Feat dice and keep the better. Ill-favoured: keep the worse. Both at once: a normal roll p.20.

Bonus and penalty diceadd or remove Success dice

Bonuses add Success dice and penalties remove them; they cancel each other out p.20 p.21.

Hope and Shadow

Hope bonus1 Hope = 1 die

Spend 1 Hope before a roll for 1 extra Success die. Once per roll p.20. At 0 Hope a hero cannot push himself p.71.

Inspired1 Hope = 2 dice

Name a Distinctive Feature that fits the roll; then 1 Hope gives 2 dice instead of 1 p.20 p.67.

Supporta friend helps

A friend with 1 or more ranks in a fitting skill spends 1 Hope: the roller gets 1 die (2 if the roller is the helper's Fellowship Focus). One helper per roll p.21 p.55.

Where Shadow comes fromfear, greed, dark magic, wrong acts

Fear (Dread): resist with Valour, Heart TN. Greed and dark magic (Sorcery): resist with Wisdom, Wits TN. Wrong acts (Misdeeds): no roll p.137 p.139.

MiserableShadow at or above Hope

While Miserable, an Eye on the Feat die fails the roll, whatever the total. It ends when Hope is above Shadow again p.22 p.71.

Shadow Scartrade Shadow for a Scar

Before Shadow reaches max Hope, a hero may swap all Shadow points for 1 Scar. A Scar counts as Shadow and goes only at Yule p.137 p.121.

Shadow at max HopeIll-favoured on everything

Shadow can never pass max Hope. When it equals it, every roll is Ill-favoured. The only way out is a bout of madness: all Shadow goes, and the hero gains a Flaw p.137 p.139 p.140.

Flawsfrom madness

A Flaw makes fitting rolls Ill-favoured p.141.

Body

Endurancestamina

Harm and hard effort lower it. At 0 the hero is knocked out for about an hour p.69.

Load and Fatigueweight and tiredness

Load = war gear and treasure carried p.49. Fatigue from journeys adds to Load for a while p.69.

WearyEndurance at or below Load

While Weary, Success dice showing 1, 2 or 3 count as 0. It ends when Endurance rises above Load again p.22 p.71.

Woundedfrom a failed Protection roll

Roll the Feat die for how bad it is: the number is the days to mend. A second Wound means Endurance 0 and Dying p.101.

Restshort rest and a night

Short rest (about an hour, once a day): Endurance back equal to Strength. A night: all of it. Wounded: nothing from a short rest, Strength from a night. At 0 Hope a night gives 1 Hope p.71.

Dyinga Healing roll within an hour

A Dying hero needs a successful Healing roll within about an hour, then wakes at 1 Endurance p.101.

Fights

Order of a fightvolleys, then rounds

First opening volleys with bows and thrown spears. Then rounds at close quarters p.94 p.95.

A roundstance, pairs, actions

Each hero picks a stance, fighters pair up, heroes act from Forward to Rearward, then the enemies. Each hero has one main and one secondary action p.95 p.97.

StancesForward, Open, Defensive, Rearward

Forward: +1 die to attack and to be attacked. Open: no change. Defensive: attacks on you lose 1 die, yours lose 1 per enemy on you. Rearward: bow only p.96. Each has a task: Intimidate Foe (Awe), Rally Comrades (Enhearten), Protect Companion (Battle), Prepare Shot (Scan) p.102 p.103.

HittingStrength TN + enemy Parry

Tom's TN to hit is his Strength TN plus the enemy's Parry. Enemies must reach Tom's Parry. A hit costs the target the weapon's Damage p.98.

Knockbackhalve one hit

Once a round, halve the Endurance lost from a hit and lose your next main action p.98 p.99.

Special damagespend icons

Heavy Blow: + Strength (+1 two-handed). Fend Off: Parry up for the round (+3 spears). Pierce: Feat die higher (+3 spears, +2 bows, +1 swords). Shield Thrust: shields only p.99.

Piercing Blow10 or rune on the Feat die

The target rolls Protection (Feat die + armour dice) against the weapon's Injury. Fail: Wounded p.99.

Leaving a fighttwo ways

Go Rearward, then leave with no roll. Or fight Defensive and use a hit to get away p.104.

Journeys

RolesGuide, Hunter, Look-out, Scout

The Company plans a route and picks roles; only one Guide p.108 p.109.

Marching teststhe Guide rolls Travel

The result says how far along the route the next event happens p.110.

Eventswho faces them

A die picks who faces each event: Scouts Explore, Look-outs Awareness, Hunters Hunting. Most events add Fatigue p.112.

Arrivinglosing Fatigue

A mount lowers Fatigue by its Vigour, then a Travel roll can lower it more. The rest goes 1 point per night of safe rest p.111.

Councils

Whena formal meeting with high stakes

A council is a big talk where much depends on the result p.104.

Resistance3, 6 or 9 successes

Set by the Loremaster, by how much the request costs the hosts p.105.

Introductionthe spokesperson rolls

Passed: tries equal to the Resistance, +1 per icon. Failed: the same tries, but failure becomes a Disaster. Reluctant hosts: −1 die; friendly: +1 die p.106.

Talking and the endicons count, roleplay helps

Each icon is one more success; good roleplay can add 1 or 2 dice. The end: success, failure (or success at a price), or Disaster p.106 p.107 p.108.

Fellowship and growing

Fellowship phaserest and recovery

Heroes spend points, get back Hope equal to Heart (all of it at Yule), may lose some Shadow, and pick undertakings p.119 p.120 p.121.

Fellowship poolshared Hope

Starts at the number of heroes plus Blessings such as Bree-blood. Spent while resting to give Hope. Full again each session p.55 p.71.

PointsSkill and Adventure points

Skill points buy skill ranks; Adventure points buy proficiencies, Valour and Wisdom. 3 of each per session; at Yule also Skill points equal to Wits p.56 p.120.

Costs4 to 30 points

A new rank costs 4, 8, 12, 20, 26, 30 points (ranks 1 to 6). One rank per ability per phase; only one of Valour or Wisdom. A new Valour rank brings a Reward, a new Wisdom rank a Virtue p.119.

Own notes in plain words. Page numbers (p.) are the printed pages of the core rulebook; the book itself is not published here.

Settings

View

Lite view is the paper look: the character sheet and the Journey Log, as on paper, still working like an app. It changes only the screen: same Tom, same journey, same notes. Each iPad keeps its own choice.

Sync and version

Starting…

Sync is off in this app. It needs your GitHub key once. Copy the key on this device (for example from your notes), then tap Paste key. Safari and the Home Screen app each need it once.

The sync file is damaged or is not a Tom save. If this device has the right Tom, send it to repair the file (the damaged file stays in the GitHub history).

Version 1.0.16Update gets the newest version and syncs now.

Tom syncs by himself, notes included: when the app opens, when you come back to it, a few seconds after each change, and every minute while it is open. Display settings, open tabs and the recent-changes list stay on each device. If two devices changed the same thing, the newer change wins and the other one is kept in Bring back.

Bring back an earlier version

Before changes from another device arrive, this device keeps a copy of what it had (the last 10).

Your GitHub key

Sync needs your own key in every app, also to read: the sync repo is private. The key is saved only in this app, never in a file of the website.

This key can read Tom and Skippy and change your website. Never share it and never paste it anywhere else.

How to make or find the key
  1. Open github.com and sign in (a computer is easiest).
  2. Your picture › Settings › Developer settings › Personal access tokens › Fine-grained tokens. Open RPG Hub sync, or Generate new token.
  3. Repository access: Only select repositories › rpghub-data in the list. Permissions › Contents › Read and write.
  4. A new key is shown only once: copy it (it starts with github_pat_).
  5. Here, tap Paste key. Once in every app on every device: Safari and the Home Screen app keep their own.
